title: Potent Activation of T Cells Using BPI-Stimulated Murine Bone Marrow-Derived Cells
author: Pfab, Christina
materials: CRITICAL: Sterile conditions must be adhered to.
CRITICAL: Adherence to sterile conditions is paramount.
Rest cells in the incubator for 3–4 h.
Sterilize the abdominal region using 70% EtOH.
Put organ(s) onto the cell strainer.
Note: Antibodies labeled with alternative fluorochrome conjugates may be used in step 12e. Please refer to Problem 5 in the troubleshooting section.
Discard pre-coat solution from the wells.

steps.title: Isolate bone marrow cells
steps.instruction: Warm sterile PBS and culture medium to 37 °C, sacrifice 12–16 week old male C57BL/6J mice by CO₂ asphyxiation or cervical dislocation, sterilize hind legs with ethanol, harvest femur and tibia (one or both legs, ~4 × 10⁷ cells per leg), remove muscle/connective tissue with sterile gauze pads, keep bones in empty tubes, draw 5 mL sterile PBS into a 5 mL syringe with a 20 G needle, replace needle with a 27 G needle, open each bone at proximal and distal ends, insert the syringe and flush marrow into a 50 mL tube, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, RT, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL medium then add 9 mL medium, count cells at 1:10 dilution, seed 4 × 10⁶ cells per petri dish in 10 mL medium containing GM‑CSF 200–400 U/mL.

steps.title: Culture BMDCs with GM‑CSF
steps.instruction: Incubate seeded bone‑marrow dishes at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in a humidified incubator; GM‑CSF concentration may be titrated for optimal differentiation (flow cytometry for CD11c⁺CD11b⁺), supernatant from GM‑CSF‑producing cells or commercial low‑endotoxin GM‑CSF may be used.

steps.title: Harvest BMDCs and generate supernatant
steps.instruction: Warm medium to 37 °C, at day 7–8 collect loose and semi‑adherent BMDCs: transfer 15 mL medium from each 30 mL‑filled petri dish into a 50 mL tube, section dish into four quarters and rinse each quarter five times with remaining medium using a 10 mL serological pipette on a fully‑charged pipet controller, pool all harvested cells (discard adherent cells), centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, RT, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL medium then add 9 mL medium, count at 1:10 dilution, adjust to 5 × 10⁵ cells mL⁻¹, plate 100 µL (5 × 10⁴ cells) per well in a flat‑bottom 96‑well plate, rest 3–4 h, stimulate 18 h with BPI at 200 nM (add 100 µL stimulation solution to reach 200 µL total per well), harvest supernatant (SN) avoiding cells, centrifuge SN 8 min at 300 × g, RT, store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Stain BMDCs for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Resuspend BMDCs in 50 µL FACS buffer containing Fc block (2 µg mL⁻¹), vortex, incubate 10 min in the dark, prepare antibody master mix: CD11c‑Vioblue (1:?) and CD11b‑VioGreen (1:50) in FACS buffer, add 50 µL master mix, vortex, incubate 30 min in the dark, add 500 µL FACS buffer, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 200 µL FACS buffer, add 5 µL 7‑AAD solution 5 min before acquisition (7‑AAD‑negative population should be >65 % CD11c⁺CD11b⁺).

steps.title: Isolate CD4+ T cells from spleen and lymph nodes
steps.instruction: Cool sterile PBS and centrifuge to 4 °C, sacrifice 8–10 week old male C57BL/6J mice by CO₂ asphyxiation or cervical dislocation, sterilize abdomen with 70 % EtOH, harvest spleen and peripheral (inguinal, axillary) lymph nodes (optional: cervical, brachial, popliteal, mesenteric), store organs in 500 µL PBS on ice, work in a laminar flow cabinet, prepare a 70 µm cell strainer, 5 mL syringe plunger and 50 mL tube, pre‑soak strainer with PBS, place organ(s) on strainer, mechanically press through with plunger, rinse plunger with 1 mL PBS into tube, wash strainer three times with 1 mL PBS, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: If spleen was used, lyse erythrocytes: discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL red‑blood‑cell lysis buffer, incubate 1 min on ice mixing gently every 15 s, add 10 mL PBS, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL PBS then add 9 mL PBS, centrifuge again 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare cells for negative MACS sort
steps.instruction: All steps on ice with MACS buffer kept at 4 °C: discard supernatant, resuspend cell pellet in 1 mL MACS buffer then add 9 mL MACS buffer, count cells at 1:10 dilution, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, add 40 µL MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells (e.g., 120 µL for 3 × 10⁷ cells), add 10 µL biotinylated antibody mix (Miltenyi CD4⁺ isolation kit) per 10⁷ cells, vortex gently, incubate 5 min on ice, add 30 µL MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells, add 20 µL anti‑biotin microbeads per 10⁷ cells, vortex gently, incubate 5 min on ice.

steps.title: Perform negative MACS isolation of CD4+ cells
steps.instruction: Prepare the MidiMACS separator (sterilize for laminar flow use), insert an LS column (MS column optional for lymph‑node cells) into the magnetic separator, equilibrate column with 3 mL MACS buffer (do not let column run dry), add the cell suspension to the column, collect all flow‑through into a fresh 50 mL tube (do not remove column during separation, do not discharge flow‑through), flush column 5 times with 1 mL MACS buffer each, centrifuge the combined flow‑through 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL medium (or MACS buffer) then add 9 mL medium (or MACS buffer), count cells (no dilution needed). Yield ≈10 % of input; purity can be checked by flow cytometry (CD3⁺CD4⁺ >97 %).

steps.title: Optional naive CD4+ T cell FACS sorting
steps.instruction: Centrifuge CD4⁺ T‑cell suspension 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 100 µL MACS buffer per 2 × 10⁶ cells, transfer to a flow‑cytometry tube, stain with CD4‑PerCP (1:100), CD62L‑PE (1:200), CD44‑FITC (1:200), CD25‑APC (1:50) using MACS buffer for dilution, incubate 30 min on ice in the dark, add 500 µL PBS, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL PBS, pass through a 30 µL pre‑separation filter into a fresh FACS tube to remove clumps, sort for CD4⁺CD62L⁺CD44⁻CD25⁻ cells (yield 30–50 % of input, purity >99 %).

steps.title: Pre‑coat 96‑well plate with αCD3
steps.instruction: Warm medium to 37 °C, add 100 µL PBS containing αCD3 antibody at 2.5 µg mL⁻¹ to each well, incubate 1 h at 37 °C (or overnight at 4 °C), discard coating solution, wash wells with 200 µL PBS (keep PBS in wells until cell suspension is ready, do not let wells dry).

steps.title: Activate and stimulate T cells with SN
steps.instruction: Centrifuge isolated CD4⁺ T cells 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, resuspend in 1 mL medium, adjust to 1.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, add αCD28 antibody to a final concentration of 8 µg mL⁻¹, aspirate PBS from pre‑coated plate, seed 100 µL cell suspension per well (1.5 × 10⁵ cells), add 100 µL BMDC‑derived SN (or 100 µL medium for a negative control; also include wells without polyclonal activation as additional controls).

steps.title: Monitor cultures and split on day 3
steps.instruction: Take daily reflected‑light microscope images to monitor cell clusters, on day 3 perform a 1:2 split: pipette cell suspension up‑and‑down five times, transfer 90 µL of the ~180 µL suspension into a fresh, non‑coated well, add 90 µL fresh BMDC‑derived SN (or 90 µL medium for a control). No further αCD3/αCD28 restimulation is required.

steps.title: Collect supernatant and harvest cells
steps.instruction: Between days 1 and 5 collect supernatant (avoid absorbing cells) and store for downstream ELISA or multiplex cytokine analysis, then harvest cells, optionally count them, and optionally perform intracellular/extracellular flow cytometry staining: CD3‑FITC (1:50), CD4‑VioGreen (1:50), CD62L‑VioBlue (1:10), CD44‑PE‑Cy7 (1:10), CD25‑APC (1:50).

steps.title: Optional flow cytometry staining of T cells
steps.instruction: Stain harvested T cells extracellularly with CD3‑FITC (1:50), CD4‑VioGreen (1:50), CD62L‑VioBlue (1:10), CD44‑PE‑Cy7 (1:10), CD25‑APC (1:50) in appropriate buffer, incubate as per antibody instructions, wash, and analyze by flow cytometry.
